sprints.title: Data Services 5 Nov
sprints.goals: This sprint aimed to standardize the user interface across all applications through a unified header component while simultaneously addressing critical data flow, permissions, and form validation issues that were blocking user workflows. The team also focused on removing technical debt and deprecated application resources to improve system maintainability and performance.
sprints.summary: The sprint delivered a comprehensive header component rollout across five applications (I/O, ITAM, RIST, TCT, and Access Requests), ensuring consistent branding and navigation for end users. The team resolved critical functional gaps including transfer workflows in the I/O application, permission controls for application configuration, form field validation issues in RIST, and debugging of position editing capabilities. Additionally, the sprint cleared deprecated screens and formulas from multiple applications, deployed TCT and ITAM updates to test environments, and completed UI mockup improvements for the Purchasing and Catalog Sync applications, collectively reducing maintenance overhead and preparing systems for production readiness.

sprints.title: Data Services 19 Nov
sprints.goals: This sprint aimed to advance core platform capabilities across multiple applications while establishing foundational architecture for dynamic data collection and cross-system interoperability. The team worked to resolve critical registration application issues, strengthen permission controls across baseline systems, and architect solutions for enhanced document management and procurement workflows.
sprints.summary: The team completed substantial feature work across five major workstreams, including critical bug fixes and UI improvements to the App Registry, architectural decisions and site preparation for the Compliance Review document management library system, permission scrubbing across three baseline list systems to strengthen security posture, and advancement of the Records API and Purchasing modules with new interface designs and packaging capabilities. Notable achievements include establishing the dynamic data collection model for Compliance Review, enabling cross-Division transfer functionality in the I/O system, and implementing improved user interfaces for Catalog Sync home screen and procurement workflows. These completions position the platform for more robust permission governance, better document handling capabilities, and improved user experience across registration and purchasing functions.

sprints.title: Data Services 3 DEC
sprints.goals: This sprint focused on stabilizing core functionality across multiple applications while advancing the Compliance Review system toward operational readiness. The team aimed to resolve critical bugs affecting notifications and environment deployments while establishing foundational features for records management and user interface consistency across the platform.
sprints.summary: The sprint delivered significant progress across five major applications with a balance of bug fixes and new capability development. Critical issues were resolved including notification routing problems in TCT, component menu errors in I/O, and environment configuration issues in Records API, while the Compliance Review application advanced with the implementation of record upload screens, metadata management interfaces, and a comprehensive security model. Supporting work included the deployment of corrected configurations to test and production environments for Regional Office, the creation of reviewer tracking in bulk processing workflows, and the establishment of automated notifications for records managers. Release documentation was prepared for both I/O and Access Requests applications to facilitate stakeholder communication and system adoption.
